source.title: How Does Learning Rate Decay Help Modern Neural Networks
source.authors: Kai-Chao You; Mingsheng Long; Jian-Min Wang; Michael I. Jordan

record.tranche_reason: The study tests learning-rate decay and memorization of added noisy data, but does not test any listed claim version about fitting completely random labels, unstructured inputs, or generalization on true labels.
record.gate_note: The study reports accuracy on noisy data in a constructed dataset, but does not state that the training labels are randomly relabeled or report fitting a completely random labeling of the training set.
record.test_reason: The study measures learning-rate-dependent fitting of unspecified noisy data and learning of simple versus complex patterns. It does not define the noise as noisy or random labels, establish a signal-before-label-memorization sequence, or report another listed claim's effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that an initially large learning rate suppresses memorization of noisy data, while learning-rate decay improves learning of complex patterns. They additionally report decreasing transferability of patterns learned in later decay stages.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines learning-rate decay on a constructed pattern dataset and noisy data; it does not reproduce the random-label experiments in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report a difference between a large learning rate followed by decay and a constant small learning rate on PS10 with 10% noise.

fits_no_version.finding: On PS10 with 10% added noisy data, an initially large learning rate with decay suppresses fitting the noisy data relative to a constant small learning rate and improves complex-pattern accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate schedules can regulate memorization of noisy examples and its interference with learning complex patterns.

record.problems: The relevant noisy-data comparison is presented in a figure without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The text does not define the added noise as random relabeling of the training set.
record.rows_left_out: Other PS10 pattern-accuracy curves and transferability results do not measure any listed claim version or the noisy-data fitting result captured in R1.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random training labels to near-zero error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Zero-error fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a random-label-corruption sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.

Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels. Figure 9 compares simple and complex signal patterns; Figure 10 compares learning-rate schedules with unspecified noisy data.

record.verdict_notes: The unspecified noise construction prevents treating Figure 10 as evidence about noisy-label memorization. This is an evidential gap, not evidence that any claim version fails.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random training-set labels, near-zero training error, chance test error, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and generalization on true labels.
Training-time comparison for true versus random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A sweep from no label corruption to all labels corrupted, perfect training fit across that sweep, and test-error trajectory.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
A comparison of learning real labels and random labels over training.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured accuracy on noisy data while comparing learning-rate decay with a constant small learning rate.

conditions.value: large learning rate with decay vs. constant small learning rate

rows.note: The authors state that the initially large learning rate suppresses fitting noisy data. The plotted values are not stated numerically in the text; the text does not specify that this is random relabeling of the training set.
rows.check: The learning-rate comparison is a valid result, but 'partial' is not justified against any claim version. Section 5.3 does not specify how noisy examples or their labels were generated. Suppressed noise-data accuracy alone does not establish V6's temporal ordering. Numerical curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
